newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-STATE COMMERCIAL BANK'S TENDER TERM PROLONGED.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-STATE COMMERCIAL BANK'S TENDER TERM PROLONGED.

text.p: Lithuania's finance ministry said on Tuesday that it will prolong the term of a public tender for the privatisation of the State Commercial Bank until August 7.
"The ministry of finance... prolongs the term of a public written tender for privatisation of the State Commercial Bank," the ministry said in an ad published in the daily Lietuvos rytas.
"All shares of the bank (100) shall be offered," the statement said.
The statement also said that the conditions and result evaluation criteria may be obtained from July 16 and the dedline to submit the applications expires on August 7.
The government announced a tender for the bank's privatisation in June but it attracted no applications by the July 1 deadline.
The finance ministry said last week it will carry out more intensive negotiations with potential investors during this month and admitted that the price tag for the bank will not be very high.
Vilniaus Bank confirmed on Monday that it was still considering investing in the bank.
The bank reported a 6.1 million litas net profit for the first half of 1997 after posting staggering losses of over 170 million litas for 1996.
The assets of the bank stood at 957.6 million litas as of end of June.
Its loan portfolio amounted to 584.1 million litas and its deposits stood at 776.2 million litas as of end of June.
